summary: These DOM IPC changes make Firefox’s multi-process browser architecture more reliable and secure: they validate file-picker and window-creation inputs, tighten principal and redirect checks, and prevent discarded or stale BrowsingContexts from being embedded or acted on. They also improve cross-process accessibility lifetimes, speech-recognition communication, streaming uploads, full-page screenshots on mobile, remote image sizing, and process identity handling. Together, the changes reduce crash and isolation risks while enabling more robust browser features across content and parent processes.
